newsitem.title: USA: Aon profits fall, takes charge for volatile securities.
newsitem.headline: Aon profits fall, takes charge for volatile securities.

text.p: Insurer Aon Corp. Tuesday reported lower second-quarter earnings after taking a $27 million special charge for losses on highly volatile securities at its Alexander & Alexander Services Inc. unit.

Aon acquired A&A in the first quarter for about $1.23 billion. But the company only discovered in the second quarter that A&A's investment portfolio contained certain highly volatile securities with previously unrecognized losses.
Aon said it immediately sold these securities, taking the charge of 10 cents a share after taxes, and launched a full financial investigation that has just been completed.

Aon said the probe revealed that A&A held certain highly volatile securities that were incorrectly classified as high quality money market instruments. These securities had been carried on A&A's books at inflated values at the time of the acquisition, it said.
The securities included inverse floater tranches of collateralized mortgage obligations, a mortgage derivative product, it added.
Aon said it contacted law enforcement authorities and is cooperating with their investigations. However, the Chicago-based company declined to comment on whether it would pursue legal action.

"Naturally, we were disappointed to uncover the securities losses, which had apparently gone undetected at A&A for several years," Patrick Ryan, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement. "But we should stress that Aon does not engage in the trading of highly volatile securities."
Aon's earnings fell to $84.2 million, or 48 cents a share, from $86.3 million, or 49 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter. Revenues rose to $1.42 billion from $932 million.
Aon Group, Aon's insurance brokerage and consulting services segment, reported second-quarter revenue growth of 99.7 percent to $923 million, due primarily to major acquisitions.
The insurance underwriting segment posted modest gains, with revenue rising 7 percent to $474 million, it said.
Aon stock edged up 12.5 cents to $54.375 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly after midday.
